scene.ofreeRecent: a Han-era inn — holds her keepsake at chest height; A secluded river bathing pavilion with sunlit limestone steps and a wicker basket for towels — She sets her folded swimming robe on a warm ledge before checking the water temperature with her toes; a training gym with a heavy bag — standing; a traditional archery ground beside a temple wall — seated on a chair; A bamboo-slip conservation studio with shallow sorting trays — She matches a broken half of a wooden tally to its mate before tying the two halves together for storage; a stage under a painted night sky of crystal stars — adjusts the height of the stand holding a microphone; a scholar's study stacked with bound bamboo slips — holds a small hand lantern low at her side; a wind-rippled desert dune trail — lying on her left side; a sunny enclosed veranda with drying racks overhead — standing; a castle kitchen with a great hearth — holds a small hand lantern low at her side; a stage under a painted night sky of crystal stars — standing with one foot up on a step; a hanfu photo studio with costume racks — perched on a ledge or edge; a vast fantasy library of towering shelves — holds her keepsake up beside her face

prompt:
INPUT: the attached image is the approved character — her Medieval fantasy card; keep her. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

CHARACTER: the same woman as the attached image — the female personification of Cao Zhi of the Three Kingdoms, seen in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye and hair colors, haircut, skin tone and body proportions; expression and hair motion may change, and her hair may be worn differently only as SCENE's Hair line says. Her medieval-fantasy identity shows ONLY as a small accessory, an object around her, or the object PROP says she holds — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never as armor, regalia or a costume.

DESIGN (accessory hints only): her legend — peerless literary genius, drunken freedom, a scroll and wine, melancholy brotherly rivalry — may inform at most one small accessory, a hair ornament or an object beside her, in its palette (deep navy blue, black lacquer, cold steel silver, ivory white). The clothes keep the chosen outfit's own colours; her skin, hair and eyes stay as in the attached image.

OBJECTS: any identity accessory or object, including the one PROP names, takes a present-day form that fits this place — a charm, a hairpin, a phone strap, a modern cup or bottle; no Chinese antique objects such as jade carvings, porcelain wine cups, bronze vessels or paper lanterns.

STYLE: Korean MMORPG character artwork. A recognisably drawn face with gently simplified anatomical structure. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.

SKIN FINISH: dewy, glass-like highlights on the skin of her shoulders, arms, collarbones and legs — a soft, luminous wet-look sheen that follows the body's forms; her face keeps a soft, natural finish.

AGE: the same adult woman as in the attached image — keep her own face shape, cheekbones, eye proportions and skin tone exactly; minimal facial lines (no nasolabial folds, crow's feet, under-eye bags or cheek creases). Keep her face soft, feminine and attractive in every framing — never elongated, gaunt, mannish or heavy-jawed, even in close-ups, profiles or low angles.

OUTPUT: one standalone off-duty scene of her in the outfit chosen in SCENE; her legend shows only through accessories and objects around her — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never as armor, regalia or a costume. Everything else follows SCENE (chosen).

FRAME: a vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) image. Compose the image for this frame; COMPOSITION in SCENE sets how much of her shows.

SCENE (chosen):
FREE DESIGN: design the place, activity, pose, framing and outfit yourself. Start from who she is — her legend, traits and personality — and show an everyday moment that is unexpected yet feels natural for her. Make it fresh through the situation and what she is doing, not through more decoration. Avoid scenes like the recent ones listed below. Keep her face, the art style and the body and anatomy rules exactly as stated. Before drawing, write your design into the lines below, then draw it. In your pose, give each hand one job only and say plainly where each arm goes; avoid poses where it is unclear which shoulder an arm comes from — an arm behind her back, behind her head or pinned under her body — and never state where a foot sits under water. Do not make it another small repair, adjusting, measuring or sorting task at a workbench, repair stall, equipment room or locker room — those scenes are already in our own list; choose another kind of everyday moment (rest, play, a meal, travel, weather, getting ready, simply being in the place).
Recent scenes to avoid: a Han-era inn — holds her keepsake at chest height; A secluded river bathing pavilion with sunlit limestone steps and a wicker basket for towels — She sets her folded swimming robe on a warm ledge before checking the water temperature with her toes; a training gym with a heavy bag — standing; a traditional archery ground beside a temple wall — seated on a chair; A bamboo-slip conservation studio with shallow sorting trays — She matches a broken half of a wooden tally to its mate before tying the two halves together for storage; a stage under a painted night sky of crystal stars — adjusts the height of the stand holding a microphone; a scholar's study stacked with bound bamboo slips — holds a small hand lantern low at her side; a wind-rippled desert dune trail — lying on her left side; a sunny enclosed veranda with drying racks overhead — standing; a castle kitchen with a great hearth — holds a small hand lantern low at her side; a stage under a painted night sky of crystal stars — standing with one foot up on a step; a hanfu photo studio with costume racks — perched on a ledge or edge; a vast fantasy library of towering shelves — holds her keepsake up beside her face.
Place: A century-old lakeside bathhouse with a dry pebble path cut between two shallow pools.
Activity: She tests the rhythm of seven skipping stones by laying them out from smallest to largest along the warm coping.
Pose: She kneels on a dry towel with her body turned slightly toward the viewer, keeping one hand on the coping while placing the smallest stone with the other.
Framing: A wide seated three-quarter portrait at pool level with the stones, both hands and her face clear.
Outfit family (required): swimwear — any swimwear outfit; you may pick one from our outfit catalog (outfit-catalog.md in this pack) or design your own, but prefer one that is not in it.
Situation (required): a situational exposure moment of your own design that fits the scene — prefer one that is not among ours: clothes soaked by rain or a splash, clothes caught by a strong gust of wind, a top worn half undone, a strap slipped off the shoulder, a hem knotted up under the bust, an outer layer tied around the waist, a sheen of sweat from heat, a backlit silhouette through thin fabric, a skirt slit fallen open, sleeves pushed up with one more button undone, a tie or scarf pulled loose.
Time of day (fixed): late morning — clear fresh daylight, soft short shadows — set your scene at this time.
Outfit: An opaque dark pine one-piece swimsuit with a braided fabric collar and a detachable pale linen side skirt. While sorting stones she folds the side skirt across the coping as a padded tray, revealing the swimsuit hip seam.
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — the chosen outfit worn in its most revealing version — a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders, a cropped or open-back cut, a short hem or high slit showing the thighs, as far as the outfit allows, skin clearly showing; intimate areas covered

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely. From the attached image take only her face, hair and body — not its garment, armor, regalia, ornaments, mecha plates or background. Dress her exactly as SCENE describes; that outfit must read at first glance, keeping its own recognisable colours and parts. Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her medieval-fantasy identity belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her faction's palette, armor, robes or regalia.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera exactly as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same. No default card pose, no default front-facing portrait.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus. Where the place is busy, other people may appear only as small, soft-focus background extras — never posed with her. No logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No readable text or numbers.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, about 7.5 heads tall — height from the legs, never a smaller head or a longer neck. The neck is a natural length and the head sits close to the shoulders. No body-part enlargement, no extra limbs.

FIGURE: keep her exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame. Right and left mean her own right and left, not the viewer's.

HANDS: natural human hands, no extra or duplicated limbs; each visible hand joins through its wrist and forearm to the matching shoulder. A hand may stay outside the crop, and fingers may be partly hidden by a grip.

AVOID: a blue or bruise-like tint on the skin around the eyes, glossy or shiny highlights on the face, sweaty, oily or plastic-looking skin.
